rule: Use consistent color purposefully throughout your interface to guide merchant attention and understanding.
quote: Color is used purposefully in our interface redesign

rule: Design type hierarchy and scale so merchants can easily find the information they need.
quote: clear do and don't examples for page layouts, designed to help merchants easily find the information they're looking for

rule: Match your interface language tone to merchant needs and emotions in each context.
quote: tone should change in order to respond to merchant needs and emotions

rule: Normalize all interaction patterns—keyboard, mouse, and callback events—into a single simple interface.
quote: normalize all the ways those events could occur (including keyboard events), and give you a simple interface for responding to them

rule: Build experiences that feel designed by the same team across all touchpoints and partners.
quote: Polaris helps everyone in building experiences that look and feel like they were designed by the same team

rule: Use a unified design language across all apps so teams feel the experience is cohesive and familiar.
quote: Across all collections, every app feels cohesive and familiar, empowering teams through one design language.

rule: Design AI experiences to be clear and useful as part of modern teamwork tools.
quote: Designing for teams today means making clear, useful AI experiences.

rule: Guide users clearly through required steps without making them figure things out alone.
quote: Guide users clearly through what they need to do. Provide direction without requiring them to figure things out themselves.

rule: Respect the user's primary task and never demand attention at moments when they cannot focus.
quote: Respect the user's primary task—in this case, driving safely. Don't demand attention at dangerous moments.

rule: Show only information relevant to the current moment; display and hide it based on need.
quote: Show only what's relevant right now. Information should appear when needed and disappear when it's not.

rule: Keep simple interactions simple; make complex tasks possible without adding unnecessary complexity.
quote: Keep the simple things simple, and make the complex things possible.

rule: Base interface patterns on how humans naturally think, not on computer architecture or implementation.
quote: Our solutions should be based on the way humans think, rather than how computers work.

rule: Respect user attention as precious; avoid interrupting them with unnecessary notifications or dialogs.
quote: The attention of our users is precious and we should guard them from unnecessary interruptions.

rule: Introduce new patterns and features mindfully, building on existing user trust and mental models.
quote: When we introduce a new pattern, we do so mindfully.

rule: Ensure every interface element contributes positively to the larger system; eliminate isolated features.
quote: Each piece is part of a greater whole and should contribute positively to the system at scale.

rule: Design products and visual language to be welcoming and accessible to global users worldwide.
quote: Our products and visual language should be welcoming and accessible.

rule: Use motion to communicate with users in ways that are easily understood and natural.
quote: Our use of motion breathes life into our products, and allows us to communicate with users in easily understood ways.

rule: Measure success by how well you fulfill human needs, not by output metrics.
quote: We measure success by how well we fulfill human needs.

rule: Build diverse teams with different skillsets and perspectives to generate more breakthrough ideas faster.
quote: By empowering people with different skillsets, backgrounds and perspectives to bring their unique points of view to the table, we generate more breakthrough ideas faster.

rule: Use low-fidelity prototypes to test hypotheses quickly and cheaply before investing in production.
quote: Rapid, low-fidelity prototyping allows us to simulate ideas and test hypotheses quickly and cheaply.

rule: Make user goals explicit in concise statements and evaluate them regularly to keep teams aligned.
quote: Hills are concise statements of the goals we aim to help our users accomplish. By making these goals explicit and evaluating them regularly, we align teams around a single shared mission.

rule: Hold regular check-ins with users and stakeholders to measure progress and uncover misalignment.
quote: Playbacks are regular check-ins that bring users, stakeholders and teams together to tell stories and exchange feedback.

rule: Align corner radii and margins around a shared center to create unified visual rhythm.
quote: By aligning radii and margins around a shared center, shapes can comfortably nest within each other.

rule: Use bolder, left-aligned typography in alerts and onboarding to strengthen clarity and readability.
quote: Typography has been refined to strengthen clarity and structure, now bolder and left-aligned to improve readability in key moments like alerts and onboarding.

rule: Ensure custom interface elements harmonize with system design language like instruments playing in the same musical key.
quote: Think of it like playing in the same music key—your interface elements should complement the system's rhythm and tone, not clash with it.

rule: Avoid nested container corners that feel too pinched or flared, as they break visual balance.
quote: keep an eye out for corners that feel too pinched— or flared. They can create tension and break the sense of balance.

rule: Choose ease-out easing for enter animations, not ease-in.
quote: An ease-in easing for an enter animation when it's supposed to be ease-out

rule: Choose semi-transparent shadows over solid borders for UI elements.
quote: they choose a solid border instead of a semi-transparent shadow for your UIs.

rule: Attend to details in every design decision; details constitute the design itself.
quote: The details are not the details. They make the design.

rule: Use design variables to enable switching between contexts like light and dark mode.
quote: Variables make it easy to switch between different contexts, like light and dark mode. When you update a variable value, the change reflects across your designs.

rule: Design gestures to mirror real-world physics and interruptibility, not require waiting for animations.
quote: Great interactions are modeled after properties from the real world, like interruptibility. This sounds silly because obviously flipping a page in a book is interruptible. But imagine if it were an animation that you had to wait for.

rule: Teach core gestures early so users unlock control of many interface parts through metaphor reuse.
quote: Great interaction design rewards learning by reusing metaphors. You can use most touch interfaces with just two gestures: tapping and swiping.

rule: Use horizontal swiping to navigate pages because humans have intuitively flipped through books for millennia.
quote: Why does swiping horizontally navigate between pages? Because that's how we've intuitively interfaced with books for thousands of years.

rule: Maintain consistent terminology and content standards across all products so users understand how to navigate your entire ecosystem.
quote: One of the most important results of this collaboration–in regard to terminology and content standards–is excellent UX writing and our ability to communicate across the entire world. We work hard to drive alignment, create robust standards and be consistent so that people can understand how to navigate our products as part of an entire ecosystem.

rule: Build complex designs from a small set of carefully selected basic elements—points, lines, and shapes—used efficiently together.
quote: Every design begins with same basic elements — points, lines, and shapes. Similarly, even the most complex designs can be reduced to these indispensable pieces. It's our belief that a great design is one where these pieces are used efficiently together.

rule: Encourage discovery through structured experimentation and play to solve old problems with new solutions.
quote: The second concept that underpinned our new icon was 'encouraging play.' We believe the way to discover new solutions to old problems is through (sometimes very structured) experimentation and play.

rule: Design with vectors and modular systems so designs adapt to any screen size or environment instead of breaking in wrong contexts.
quote: An example of this is designing with vectors rather then pixels. If you can create a design that is made up of a ruleset, it can adapt to any environment. If you design with a fixed set of pixels, they're bound to break down in the wrong context.

rule: Standardize repeated elements (typography sizes, spacing, colors) into one style instead of maintaining multiple near-identical versions.
quote: We also looked for elements that were similar, but not exactly the same, and agreed on one style. So, instead of 12 different sizes for headings, we established an H1-H3, body copy, and technical copy styles.

rule: Update design system components once in a central location so changes propagate across all pages without hunting through code.
quote: Additionally, when we want to make a universal change to an atom or molecule, we can do it once in Contentful, rather than getting a developer to hunt through every page to make dozens of updates directly.

rule: Break out of the design system for exceptional focal points (like homepage hero animations) that don't repeat elsewhere.
quote: There are also times when we break out of the system. For example, we wanted to capture a visitor's attention right away on our homepage, so we opted for larger, centered headline that is animated. There are no other sections like this on our site and therefore this is not part of our design system.

rule: Design mobile-first because most online store traffic occurs on mobile devices.
quote: Most online store traffic is on mobile, so design for mobile devices first.

rule: Match the appearance and behaviors of the Shopify admin to build merchant trust across workflows.
quote: the best apps provide merchants with a user experience that matches the appearance and behaviors of the Shopify host surface. This consistency builds merchant trust

rule: Prioritize merchant needs over visual differentiation to create a better experience.
quote: put merchant needs ahead of being different for its own sake

rule: Build with accessibility best practices so the app works for all merchants and their customers.
quote: Build with accessibility best practices so your app works for all merchants and their customers.

rule: Use Polaris components to ensure your app evolves with the Shopify admin.
quote: By using Polaris, your app can evolve with us.

rule: Use the fewest details needed to make illustrations instantly recognizable at a glance.
quote: using the fewest details needed to get the point across. Not enough details, and learners might be confused. Too many, and shapes could be less readable at a glance

rule: Frame artwork with white negative space so each illustration enhances the app experience and never interrupts it.
quote: framed with white negative space and constructed of clever, clearly recognizable details so each illustration enhances our learners' app experience, and never interrupts it

rule: Use exaggeration and humor in visual design to reduce learner intimidation and encourage daily practice.
quote: When the visuals are playful, the intimidation falls away, and learners actually look forward to coming back to practice every day

rule: Rotate lines and angles in artwork to direct the eye toward UI elements or text that needs attention.
quote: To draw attention to UI or text on the screen, we rotate lines and angles in the artwork to direct the eye

rule: Balance consistency with purpose; avoid consistency patterns that lack function or occupy space without signaling value.
quote: using artwork in every tab header is consistent, but it can also feel forced, especially if it occupies significant space without signaling anything useful

rule: Balance simplicity with clarity; remove elements strategically but retain what users need to understand the interface.
quote: Simplicity is good but not at the expense of clarity. Good design means knowing what to remove and what to keep

rule: Use tiered header sizes based on each tab's purpose while keeping titles consistently positioned across tabs.
quote: we created tiered sizes based on each tab's purpose while keeping the titles consistently positioned

rule: Design layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and are aware of the platform to make experiences feel natural.
quote: A layout that adapts to different screen sizes and is aware of the platform it's on makes an experience feel natural

rule: Reduce visual clutter and noise to keep people centered, calm, and confident in their work.
quote: Less visual clutter and noise keeps people centered, calm, and confident

rule: Include people with diverse abilities and perspectives early in design to generate better solutions and help people feel they belong.
quote: Including and learning from a variety of people with a range of abilities and perspectives earlier in the design process makes for better solutions

rule: Focus design energy on signature experiences that connect products together and give them a distinctively recognizable feel.
quote: We focus our energy on signature experiences that connect our products together and give them a distinctively Microsoft feel

rule: Design visually by moving things around and testing relationships; the act of doing builds clarity instead of assuming it.
quote: Working visually keeps me close to the problem and is slow enough gives me time to think while I work. Moving things around, testing relationships, and refining structure is not separate from the thinking

rule: Keep styles colocated with components for developer clarity, not separated into distant files.
quote: Styles stay colocated with components, the API is small, and style resolution is deterministic

rule: Define styling foundations—variables, constants, and shared primitives—before scaling a large migration.
quote: Before the codemod could do useful work, we had to define the StyleX variables, constants, and shared primitives

rule: Give coding agents narrow scopes, codemods, examples, validation scripts, and checklists to succeed in large migrations.
quote: Agents work better when they have a narrow scope, a codemod runner, examples, validation scripts, and a clear checklist

rule: Make navigation and supporting elements visually recede so the main content area—where users work—takes precedence.
quote: The navigation sidebar used to appear bright enough that it remained visually prominent even after a user had reached their destination. In the updated interface, it's a few notches dimmer, allowing the main content area—where users work—to take precedence

rule: Reduce icon usage, scale down their sizes, and remove unnecessary visual treatments like colored backgrounds.
quote: The refresh reduces icon usage, scales their sizes down, and removes unnecessary visual treatments like colored team icon backgrounds

rule: Round separator edges and soften contrast to provide structure without visual clutter.
quote: By rounding out their edges and softening the contrast, the polished interface gives users structure on the page without cluttering their view

rule: Shift default color palettes toward warmer grays that feel crisp without high saturation to avoid a muddy appearance.
quote: The old palette was a cool, blue-ish hue, and the aim was to inch toward a warmer gray that still feels crisp, but less saturated

rule: Express design decisions in a platform-agnostic way so they can be shared across different disciplines, tools, and technologies.
quote: Design tokens are a methodology for expressing design decisions in a platform-agnostic way so that they can be shared across different disciplines, tools, and technologies.

rule: Help establish a common vocabulary for design decisions across organizations.
quote: They help establish a common vocabulary across organizations.

rule: Use consistent design tokens across all artifact types and surfaces to maintain on-brand consistency.
quote: The same design tokens applied across artifact kinds — a website, an app, a slide, a poster. Original mocks re-skinned with this system, not screenshots.

rule: Prefer tinted background washes over borders to delineate surfaces and reduce visual noise.
quote: Borders are rare — Arc prefers tinted background washes ( rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5) over the gradient) to delineate panes.

rule: Conduct regular accessibility audits using WCAG guidelines to identify and fix compliance gaps.
quote: This checklist uses the The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines ( WCAG ) as a reference point.

rule: Use a consistent grid position across pages to reduce layout shift perception and show rendering performance.
quote: Having a consistent grid position across all pages as a user navigates through helps the user see what content swaps out, and how quickly. It lessens the appearance of a pseudo layout shift happening between views

rule: Set line length to 14–16px text width via grid column sizing for optimal readability.
quote: At 1080 wide, the grid also helps each column of 360 have a readable line-length for 14-16px text

rule: Use two-column layouts for better navigation through long-form content.
quote: Two column layouts offer better navigation through long-form content

rule: Use a grab handle micro-interaction to signal movability without persistent toolbars or overlays.
quote: The six-dot grab handle that appears on hover is a deliberate micro-interaction worth noting. It signals movability across every block type without a persistent toolbar

rule: Add icons and emoji to navigation items to reduce cognitive load through spatial memory.
quote: Page icons and emoji turn navigation into a visual index. Users develop spatial memory for their workspace because every page has a distinct visual marker, reducing the cognitive load

rule: Use progressive disclosure in sidebars to scale from simple to deeply nested structures.
quote: The sidebar never shows more depth than the user has created: a new user with five pages sees a clean list; a power user with 200 nested pages across 12 project folders sees a structured tree

rule: Build React components with accessibility as a core feature, not an afterthought.
quote: Each component is implemented with accessibility in mind. The result is a set of accessible-by-default components, over what is possible from plain Bootstrap.

rule: Use semantic design tokens to streamline and centralize design decisions across your system.
quote: Tokens . Streamline design decisions with semantic tokens

rule: Prioritize dark mode as a built-in feature, not an optional add-on.
quote: Dark mode support looks amazing and it is 100% built-in.

rule: Apply consistent focus styling across all interactive components for accessible keyboard navigation.
quote: I love the consistent use of focus styling and the subtle animation.

rule: Build composable components with thoughtful defaults that users can customize and extend.
quote: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.

rule: Support responsive design by allowing breakpoint prefixes on any utility class.
quote: just throw a screen size in front of literally any utility to apply it at a specific breakpoint.

rule: Support multiple language text directions using logical properties instead of fixed left/right.
quote: Supporting multiple language text directions is no longer a nightmare.

rule: Use CSS layers to manage specificity automatically without developer burden.
quote: Tailwind uses CSS layers so you don't have to worry about specificity issues.

rule: Create a design system to reduce redundancy and establish visual consistency at scale.
quote: A design system is a complete set of standards intended to manage design at scale using reusable components and patterns.

rule: Reuse premade UI components to replicate designs quickly and reduce inconsistency risk.
quote: The primary benefit of design systems is their ability to replicate designs quickly by utilizing premade UI components and elements.

rule: Document design system usage explicitly to ensure consistent application across teams.
quote: Any design system, even if it were adapted from an existing one, needs instructions for use — otherwise there is a risk that it may be applied inconsistently or incorrectly across screens or across teams.

rule: Model interactions on real-world metaphors users already understand intuitively.
quote: Great interactions are modeled after properties from the real world, like interruptability.

rule: Trigger lightweight actions during a swipe gesture, not just at release, for immediate feedback.
quote: Lightweight actions, such as displaying overlays, feel more natural to trigger during the swipe after an arbitrary amount of distance.

rule: Teach users interaction patterns through reusable metaphors that compound as they explore.
quote: Great interaction design rewards learning by reusing metaphors. You can use most touch interfaces with just two gestures: tapping and swiping.

rule: Distinguish primary actions visually from secondary actions to guide users toward task completion.
quote: visually distinguish primary and secondary actions so people have an clear path illuminating their primary goal

rule: Make secondary actions recede visually to prevent accidental errors, even if users must search slightly longer to find them.
quote: Reducing the visual prominence of secondary actions minimizes the risk for potential errors and further directs people toward a successful outcome
finding: Option A (link-style Cancel) achieved 100% success with zero errors; users valued preventing accidental cancellation over speed.

rule: Align form action buttons to the left when form controls above are also left-aligned to reduce eye-travel distance.
quote: left-alignment of these two options is the best design choice – especially when the form controls above are also left aligned
finding: Left-aligned buttons (Options A, B, C) were most effective; Option E (right-aligned) caused 6 users to mistakenly click Cancel and was ~6 seconds slower.

rule: Use contrasting colors on secondary buttons to make the primary action stand out, accepting minor efficiency trade-offs.
quote: people responded well to designs that made 'Cancel' stand out in some way – even if these designs slowed them down a little
finding: Option C (grey Cancel button) increased fixations by ~8 compared to Option B, but users preferred it to prevent data loss.

rule: Design layouts that adapt to multiple viewport sizes and input modes rather than creating separate experiences for each device.
quote: Rather than tailoring disconnected designs to each of an ever-increasing number of web devices, we can treat them a

rule: Accept that the web is transient and flexible; embrace layouts that adapt rather than imposing fixed constraints.
quote: We should embrace the fact that the web doesn't have the same constraints, and design for this flexibility

rule: Limit options to prevent user overwhelm when presenting choices in an interface.
quote: The tendency for people to get overwhelmed when they are presented with a large number of options

rule: Group related information together to reduce cognitive load and aid comprehension.
quote: A process by which individual pieces of an information set are broken down and then grouped together in a meaningful whole

rule: Respond to user input within 400ms to maintain productivity and interaction flow.
quote: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that neither has to wait on the other

rule: Position targets large and close together to reduce selection time per Fitts's Law.
quote: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target

rule: Reduce decision time by decreasing the number and complexity of choices available.
quote: The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices

rule: Maintain consistency with familiar patterns users encounter on other established sites.
quote: Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know

rule: Group elements with clear visual boundaries to help users perceive them as related.
quote: Elements tend to be perceived into groups if they are sharing an area with a clearly defined boundary

rule: Place related elements near each other to help users perceive them as grouped.
quote: Objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together

rule: Simplify ambiguous designs into the simplest form to reduce cognitive effort required.
quote: People will perceive and interpret ambiguous or complex images as the simplest form possible, because it is the interpretation that requires the least cognitive effort

rule: Use visual similarity to help users perceive related elements as a complete group.
quote: The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if those elements are separated

rule: Connect related elements visually to signal their relationship more strongly.
quote: Elements that are visually connected are perceived as more related than elements with no connection

rule: Limit working memory load to seven items plus or minus two when presenting lists.
quote: The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory

rule: Choose the simplest solution among competing design approaches that achieve equal results.
quote: Among competing hypotheses that predict equally well, the one with the fewest assumptions should be selected

rule: Design without assumption users will read documentation; make interfaces self-explanatory.
quote: Users never read manuals but start using the software immediately

rule: Focus on the peak moment and conclusion of an experience; users judge these most heavily.
quote: People judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak and at its end, rather than the total sum or average of every moment

rule: Accept flexible user input while sending consistent, well-formed responses.
quote: Be liberal in what you accept, and conservative in what you send

rule: Show only the most important options initially; defer advanced features to secondary screens.
quote: Initially, show users only a few of the most important options. Offer a larger set of specialized options upon request.

rule: Keep field labels visible outside form fields; use placeholder text only as supplementary information.
quote: Labels outside the form fields make the essential information visible at all times, while placeholder text inside form fields is reserved for supplementary information.

rule: Large text (18pt or 14pt bold) requires only 3:1 contrast ratio; smaller text requires 4.5:1.
quote: Large text is easier to read, so the contrast requirement is reduced to 3:1. WCAG defines large text as text that is 18pt and larger, or 14pt and larger if it is bold.

rule: Make the Back button return to the previous screen, not up the hierarchy, so it matches user expectations.
quote: The Back button is a long-standing essential in browser navigation. Over time, users have built a strong mental model for it: namely, Back is supposed to lead back to the previous screen, essentially acting as an undo.

rule: Test your design with realistic users performing realistic tasks to uncover actual usability problems.
quote: Even the best UX designers can't design a perfect — or even good enough — user experience without iterative design driven by observations of real users and of their interactions with the design.

rule: Test only one design element at a time to isolate which change drives the improvement.
quote: Ideally, the variant should differ from the original design only in one design element alone, such as a button, an image, or a description.

rule: Base your A/B test hypothesis on user research and business insights to increase success likelihood.
quote: Before getting started on an A/B test, you should come up with a hypothesis for which changes might have which impact. As stated above, the more this hypothesis is based on user research and business insights, the higher the likelihood that your A/B test will be successful and meaningful.

rule: Make toggle switches deliver results immediately without requiring users to click Save or Submit.
quote: Toggle switches should take immediate effect and should not require the user to click Save or Submit to apply the new state.
